Settings and performance

In a world, press Esc and choose Settings; on the start menu, choose Settings directly. Most preferences follow you between worlds.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 6 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Open the settings

  1. In a world, press Esc and choose Settings. On the start menu, choose Settings directly. Ctrl+F on the pause menu opens Settings with search ready.
  2. Choose Graphics, Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Interface or Advanced, then a subpage.
  3. Click Find settings or press Ctrl+F, then type. A setting matches when every word appears in its group, page, name or help. Enter or Tab leaves the field; Up/Down then steps through matches on every page. Ctrl+Backspace clears the search.
Key or actionWhat it does
Tab / Shift+TabNext / previous group.
Page Up / Page DownPrevious / next subpage; on Key bindings, previous / next page of actions.
Up / Down arrowsSelect a row or search result.
Left / Right arrows, or EnterStep the selected value back / forward.
Click a chip or < >, drag a sliderSet a value directly.
Right-click a rowStep its value backward.
Backspace / Reset pageRestore this page’s defaults, outside text entry. On Key bindings, Backspace or Reset keys restores every key.

Changes apply immediately. Hover a label for help. Back or Esc returns to the pause menu or start menu; Resume returns to play. Local play pauses; connected servers continue. Settings menu basics

Graphics, controls and interface

  • Graphics > Display holds Graphics preset, Field of view, Horizon distance, Atmospheric fog, Frame limit, Shader and Chunk fade-in.
  • Graphics preset sets five of them at once. Low: Shader None, 32 chunks, Dense fog, no fade-in, 60 FPS. Balanced (the defaults): Fast, 64 chunks, Balanced fog, fade-in, 60 FPS. High: Fast, 128 chunks, Balanced fog, fade-in, 120 FPS. Cinematic: Cinematic, 192 chunks, Light fog, fade-in, 60 FPS. Editing one of those five shows Custom; Field of view is not part of a preset.
  • Shader offers None, Fast (default) or Cinematic. None is plain voxel lighting; Fast adds sun shadows, sun rays and haze; Cinematic refines shadows and rays and adds reflective water, at extra frame time. Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic
  • Horizon distance offers 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 (default), 96, 128, 192, 256, 512 and 1024 chunks. One chunk is 16 m; the largest radius is about 16 km. It sets only the low-detail distant view; full-detail terrain near you stays at nine chunks. Horizon distance
  • Frame limit is 60 (default), 120, 240 or Unlimited. A cap is not a guaranteed frame rate. There is no separate vsync setting; Frame limit paces the frames. Frame limit
  • Atmospheric fog is Light, Balanced (default) or Dense; haze strength follows Horizon distance. Field of view is 60–96° in 2° steps (default 72°). Chunk fade-in (on by default) fades newly loaded terrain in over 0.6 seconds. Atmospheric fog (haze) presets Field of view Chunk fade-in
  • Controls > Mouse has separate Horizontal and Vertical sensitivity (50–200% in 10% steps, default 100%) and Invert mouse Y.
  • Controls > Key bindings changes gameplay keys. Select an action and press Enter (or click it), then press the new key. Esc cancels and Delete leaves the action unbound. Esc, F6, F11 and Print Screen cannot be assigned. A key used by two actions shows “Conflict: …”. Defaults are in Controls reference.
  • Gameplay > Movement has Camera bob, Speed FOV, Damage bob (Off, Reduced or Full) and Hold/Toggle for Sprint, Sneak and Crawl. Sprint and Sneak default to Hold; Crawl defaults to Toggle.
  • Interface > Layout has GUI size (Auto, Small, Normal or Large), UI scale (75–200% in 5% steps), HUD text only, Target info (F2), HUD compass and Compact map heading. Scale is capped so the menu fits. GUI size
  • Interface > Crosshair sets style (Cross, Dot or Brackets), size (50–200%), colour (Adaptive, White, Lime or Cyan) and opacity (25–100%). Every style keeps accuracy feedback.
  • Interface > Accessibility has Color vision palettes for information overlays, High contrast, Reduce motion, Low survival warning and Warning pulse. The warning appears when health, food, water or stamina falls to 10, 20, 30 or 40% (default 20%). Reduce motion turns off camera bob, FOV kick, blast shake, fades and pulses; static warnings remain.

Sound and music

  • Audio > Volume has Master, Music, Effects, Ambience and UI volume, each 0–100% (default 100%). Arrow keys move them 5% at a time. Master scales every category; zero on one category mutes only that category. Master volume
  • Audio > Music turns music on or off, sets Music speed from 0.5× to 2.0× in 0.1× steps (tempo and pitch; effects keep their speed) and picks the Previous or Next song. Below it you see the current title, “No music installed”, or a sound problem: “Sound unavailable: install alsa-utils” on Linux, or “install ffplay (FFmpeg)” on Windows and macOS. Music: on/off, speed and song choice

Set Ambience volume to zero to silence nature sounds while keeping effects and music. Nature sounds continue behind in-world menus but stop underwater and on the start menu. Nature ambience

Diagnostics

Advanced > Diagnostics has LOD view, Voxel view, Distant terrain, Performance, Chunk borders and FPS and coordinates; Mesh view is shown as unavailable. The FPS box is on by default and shows measured FPS with the limit (or UNCAPPED), your X, Y and Z position and the biome. It hides while a menu is open. FPS and coordinates readout

Key or actionWhat it does
F3Show or hide the performance overlay: CPU work over the last half second, frame time against the frame budget, the worst recent frame and a spike count. The budget follows Frame limit (Unlimited uses 60 FPS); a spike is a frame longer than both 25 ms and twice the budget.
F7Show or hide 16 m chunk borders. Your current chunk is gold; neighbours are cyan.
F8Cycle the LOD view: Off, Tint and Colors. With the standard palette, cyan is full detail; green, blue, yellow, orange, purple and red mark the 0.5 to 16 m distant stages.
F9Turn all three overlays off if any is on; otherwise turn all on, with LOD view in Tint.
Tip. The keys above are defaults and can be reassigned. Performance, Chunk borders and LOD view are not saved: after a restart they are off, and the FPS box is on again. Chunk borders (F7), LOD view (F8) and all diagnostics (F9) Performance overlay (F3)
  • Voxel view: Off (default), Edges, which tints every block border, or X-ray, which draws only the outlines. Voxel view: block edges and X-ray outlines
  • Distant terrain: on by default. It draws the low-detail horizon beyond the nearby chunks. Turning it off saves work on slow machines. The view then ends at the nearby loaded terrain, where new chunks appear as you move. Distant terrain on/off

If the game runs slowly

  1. Try Graphics > Display > Graphics preset > Low: plain shading, 32-chunk horizon, dense fog, no terrain fade and a 60 FPS limit.
  2. If needed, lower Horizon distance to 16 or 8 chunks, or turn Advanced > Diagnostics > Distant terrain off. The distant view becomes shorter.
  3. Use the default F3 key to compare frame time with the frame budget. Compare the same place and settings before drawing conclusions.

The normal window does not provide live GPU pass timings. This guide has no current hardware benchmark or promised frame-rate gain. Performance overlay (F3)

Which settings follow you

Graphics, audio, interface preferences and key bindings follow the player between worlds. They save automatically about half a second after a change and when you quit; on Linux the file is ~/.config/voxelgame/settings. If it cannot be read, the game leaves it untouched, stops saving preferences and shows “Settings not saved …”; fix the file and restart. Time, weather and season belong to each world, under Gameplay > World; they are read-only in survival. For profile locations and recovery, see Install, update and find your worlds. World controls and shared preferences

Current limits

Good to know. The 1024-chunk horizon is available as an optional distant view. No current hardware performance result is supplied here. 1024-chunk horizon (about 16 km)
Planned, not in the game. Live GPU pass timings in ordinary play remain planned. The normal window’s GPU box reports unavailable. Live GPU timing in the performance overlay
Good to know. The native app requests that the desktop stay awake while its window is focused and visible, including menus. Desktop support varies; it releases the request on focus loss or hiding. Keep the display awake while playing

How this guide was checked

Every Settings group, page, option name, range, default and help text, the graphics presets, search and reset, key capture, the F3/F7/F8/F9 overlays, audio mixing, nature-ambience rules and the shared preference file were re-checked against Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480 source on 2026-11-08. Normal-window GPU timing remains separate from offscreen developer profiling.
